editorial:
Imagine stepping back into the neon glow of the eighties and nineties with one of the most creative pop bands from Norway. You get to see a-ha not just as musicians, but as visual artists who changed how music videos looked. This collection is a total blast because it brings together 16 of their best tracks, mixing their catchy synth-pop sound with wild imagery. It feels like a high-energy time capsule that captures the band at their peak, guided by director Steve Barron who knew exactly how to make their songs look as good as they sounded.

What really pops here is the animation and the experimental style of the videos, especially the legendary Take On Me. The pacing is quick, so you never get bored while jumping from one hit to the next. While it is more of a video companion than a traditional movie with a plot, it is a goldmine for anyone who loves pop history.
endingExplained: Since this is a music documentary and video collection, it does not have a plot twist. It wraps up by cycling through the band's greatest hits and showing the evolution of their style. The final scenes leave you with a feeling of nostalgia, closing out with their most iconic songs. It ends by celebrating the band's legacy and their impact on music videos, leaving you wanting to go back and watch the whole thing again.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s pop and creative music videos.
